title: Tor amplitude bounds tensor cohomology below
statement: Let $C$ be a braided closed monoidal Grothendieck abelian category whose tensor is additive in each variable, with functorial flat resolutions and a chosen derived category $D(C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Equip $D(C)$ with the K-flat derived tensor product. An object of $C$ is flat when tensoring with it is exact. For $K\in D(C)$ and integers $a,b$, say that $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ when $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}F[0])=0$ for every $F\in C$ and every $i<a$ or $b<i$. Let $N\in D(C)$ and $c\in\mathbf Z$ with $H^i(N)=0$ for $i<c$. Then $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for $i<a+c$. The flat model is the one of [lem-sc-source-tor-amplitude-flat-model].

source.place: DerivedCategory.isGE_tensor_of_torAmplitudeIn; bounded flat model and derived tensor bounds, cf. Stacks Tags 0654 and 06Y7

proof.text: Represent K by a bounded flat model S in [a,b] and N by a complex M vanishing below c. S is K-flat. In total degrees less than a+c each tensor summand has S-index below a or M-index below c, so it is zero. The total tensor therefore has zero terms and cohomology below a+c. Transport this through the K-flat derived tensor comparison. This is FlatModel.lean:453-461.
